_comment: Claude Code settings shared by the team (versioned). Personal preferences — plugins, exemptions — go into .claude/settings.local.json, gitignored. MODEL: an allowed shell verb is NOT necessarily harmless — a verb's sub-options (git -c core.sshCommand=…, git --upload-pack=…, find -exec, rg --pre) escalate an allowed verb into arbitrary command execution. So: allow for the verbs really used every day, ask for what rewrites history or touches the outside world, deny for the dangerous sub-options. Evaluation order: deny → ask → allow, first match wins; deny ALWAYS beats allow. The git denies neutralise the known levers of arbitrary execution (--upload-pack / --receive-pack run a command on the "remote" side, --ext-diff, --exec-path, and the catch-all '-c <key>=<value>' that covers core.sshCommand / core.pager / core.fsmonitor / protocol.ext / alias=!cmd) — at the cost of also blocking a benign 'git -c user.email=…', which is acceptable here. This '-c' is refused when it directly follows git ('git -c *'), not anywhere: a '*' replaces any text, and a 'git *-c *' pattern also refused creating a branch or reusing a commit message, options of the subcommand. Placed after another global option (git -C dir -c …), it matches no allow, all subcommand prefixes: Claude asks for approval. defaultMode 'default' already makes Claude ask for any unlisted Bash. NOTE: never put a bare 'Bash' in 'ask' — it matches every command and would make the allows below unreachable. NOTE: shell metacharacters (| ; && $() ``) CANNOT be handled here: Claude Code splits a compound command on the operators and matches each subcommand, so the operator never appears in the matched string and a 'Bash(*|*)' rule never matches. That is the role of the PreToolUse hook .claude/hooks/bash-guard.mjs, which sees the raw command and makes Claude ask for approval (never a flat refusal) on a secrets file or a pipe into a shell; the Read(…) rules of 'ask' cover reading the same files with the Read, Grep and Glob tools, which the Bash hook does not see. The .claude/hooks/scope-reminder.mjs hook applies scoping on the agent side: in PreToolUse it refuses writing a code file outside any brief when .drwil/ia-first.json -> scopeReminder is "blocking" (default); in PostToolUse it only emits a reminder in "warning" (docs/projects/kit-mechanics.md). Stack commands (allow): added automatically from the technology detected at install time (STACK_ALLOW in the kit's source code); to complete by hand for an unrecognised stack.
